sonal-cs: Heads up — Acme reports Feb invoice totals ~18% higher than the dashboard during the month-close. Dashboard shows ~1,200,412 tokens, invoice line shows 1,420,900. They were on Growth (pro-2) whole month. Can we triage?

ben-eng: Can you paste the account_id and a sample invoice line? Also confirm whether tokens are generation vs embeddings.

sonal-cs: account_id=acct_0GJ2XYZ sample_invoice_line='pro-2|2025-02-01:2025-02-28|tokens:1,420,900|amount:$X' — customer says dashboard totals match what they see in console.

ben-eng: OK. First checks: run a metering sum across the whole month and also check raw events near the cutoff. Quick metering SQL to run against metering.events:
```
SELECT sum(tokens) as total_tokens
FROM metering.events
WHERE account_id='acct_0GJ2XYZ'
  AND event_ts >= '2025-02-01'
  AND event_ts < '2025-03-01';
```

billing-bot: Snapshot export available: s3://redwood-billing-snaps/2025-02-28/acct_0GJ2XYZ/snapshot.csv :white_check_mark:

sonal-cs: Ran the sum -> total_tokens = 1,200,412 (matches dashboard).

ben-eng: If metering.events matches dashboard but invoice is higher, two likely causes: 1) ledger ingestion/backfill duplicated events, 2) invoice uses ledger postbacks + proration/reserved burst allocation at cutoff. Can you check raw_events around 2025-02-28 23:55 to 2025-03-01 00:05 for duplicates? Use this query to find duplicates by event_id:
```
SELECT event_id, count(*) as c, min(event_ts), max(event_ts)
FROM metering.raw_events
WHERE account_id='acct_0GJ2XYZ'
  AND event_ts >= '2025-02-28 23:55:00'
  AND event_ts < '2025-03-01 00:05:00'
GROUP BY event_id
HAVING c > 1;
```

sonal-cs: Found 7 duplicated event_id values. The duplicates were inserted by backfill_job_3 which ran at 2025-03-01 00:01:12 (during cutoff). Total duplicated tokens sum ~220,488.

olivia-fin: That delta (~220k tokens) explains the invoice jump. Can you attach the evidence (query results + snapshot) and we can process a credit.

ben-eng: Root cause appears to be the backfill job re-running overlapping window because the job lock failed at cutover. The ingest pipeline currently does plain INSERTs without idempotency checks, so retries create duplicate raw events. Proposed mitigation: add dedupe by raw_event_id (UPSERT or INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING), re-run a dedupe backfill to rebuild ledger lines, and mark this invoice for adjustment.

sam-support: :eyes: Do we have an ETA for the dedupe and for finance to issue the credit so I can tell Acme?

olivia-fin: I'll approve a one-time credit for the 220,488 tokens. I'll post an adjustment journal and generate a corrected invoice by EOD. Please include the CSV evidence from s3 and the SQL output.

ben-eng: Quick remediation steps for eng: 1) patch ingest job to use upserts (PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/ingest/commit/abc123), 2) run dedupe backfill on raw_events for acct_0GJ2XYZ, 3) recompute ledger lines and export new invoice snapshot. I can run the backfill now with a safeguard dry-run first.

olivia-fin: Logged FIN-2025-042 for tracking — credit issued pending backfill verification.

sonal-cs: I'll draft the customer message: explain a duplicate backfill during cutoff caused ~220k duplicate tokens; we've adjusted the invoice and will send the corrected one. Sharing the customer-friendly wording in #customer-updates before sending.

ben-eng: After backfill completes we'll confirm numbers match dashboard. PR has tests for idempotency. :white_check_mark:

sonal-cs: Thanks all — updating Acme now. Closing loop once finance confirms the updated invoice. :tada:
